candidates.exact_span: EPA-approved test procedures (methods) for the analysis and quantification of pollutants or pollutant parameters, including for the purposes of compliance monitoring/DMR reporting, permit renewal applications, or any other reporting that may be required as a condition of this permit, shall be sufficiently sensitive.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a method qualifies as sufficiently sensitive for compliance monitoring/DMR reporting affects which monitoring obligations apply (B) and whether reported measurements support enforceable numeric limit comparisons versus report-only or non-comparable monitoring (A).

candidates.exact_span: A method is "sufficiently sensitive" when (1) the method minimum level (ML) of quantification is at or below the level of the applicable effluent limit for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter; or (2) if there is no EPA-approved analytical method with a published ML at or below the effluent limit (see table below), then the method has the lowest published ML (is the most sensitive) of the analytical methods approved under 40 CFR Part 136 or required under 40 CFR Chapter I, Subchapters N or O, for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter; or (3) the method is specified in this permit or has been otherwise approved in writing by the permitting authority (EPA Region 6) for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Prong (1) ties method quantification to the applicable effluent limit, so its interpretation can change whether a numeric limit applies to a measurement or whether exceedance can be determined (A) and how sub-ML or qualified results are classified (C). Prong (2) governs method choice when no published ML meets the limit, affecting monitoring obligations (B) and whether numeric compliance comparison remains applicable (A,C). Prong (3) can substitute permit- or authority-approved methods, changing which monitoring method requirements apply (B).

candidates.exact_span: The Permittee has the option of developing and submitting a report to justify the use of matrix or sample-specific MLs rather than the published levels. Upon written approval by EPA Region 6 the matrix or sample-specific MLs may be utilized by the Permittee for all future Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR) reporting requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether matrix or sample-specific MLs were approved in writing changes the effective quantification level for DMR reporting (B), which in turn can change whether reported values are comparable to effluent limits (A) and whether absent or qualified results reflect documented no-data states versus inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Current EPA Region 6 minimum quantification levels (MQLs) for reporting and compliance are provided in Appendix A of Part II of this permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The cross-reference to Appendix A MQLs for both reporting and compliance can change which quantification thresholds govern monitoring obligations (B) and which reported measurements are subject to numeric limit comparison (A), depending on how Appendix A values are read against effluent limits.

candidates.computation_change_reason: Which pollutants are specified as lacking methods with ML at or below the effluent limit determines when prong (2) of the sufficiently-sensitive test applies, affecting required monitoring methods (B), whether numeric compliance comparison is applicable for those parameters (A), and how missing or non-quantifiable results should be classified (C).
